claim: The bare ありません front has two meanings the learner knows (there isn't / do not have) and the card accepts only 'Do not have', while its base card arimasu-have carries a hint that this conjugated form lacks.
evidence: Recognition front: 'ありません' with no hint; back 'Answer: Do not have'. Lesson 12 taught あります as 'Be, exist' and なにもありません as 'There is nothing'; arimasu-have's front adds 'about owning something'.
fix: Add the same hint as arimasu-have ('about owning something') to the Recognition face.
verdictReason: No hint on either face; the base card arimasu-have carries 'about owning something' because あります already means 'be, exist' from Lesson 12, and the ledger's only ありません is なにもありません 'There is nothing', so the bare front reads either way. Same hint on the conjugated forms is the consistent fix.

claim: The bare ありました front reads as 'there was' to a learner who met it in Lesson 13, but the card wants 'Had', and nothing on the front says possession.
evidence: Recognition front: 'ありました' with no hint; back 'Answer: Had'. Ledger: えんぴつはつくえのうえにありました 'The pencil was on the desk.', きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありました 'Last year there was a convenience store in front of the station.'
fix: Add the hint 'about owning something', matching arimasu-have.
verdictReason: Ledger teaches ありました only as 'was / there was' (えんぴつはつくえのうえにありました, きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありました, かぎはひきだしのなかにありました); the card has no hint and wants 'Had'.

claim: The bare ありませんでした front reads as 'there wasn't' from Lesson 12-13, but the card wants 'Did not have', with no hint.
evidence: Recognition front: 'ありませんでした'; back 'Answer: Did not have'. Ledger: きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありませんでした 'Last year there was no convenience store in front of the station.'
fix: Add the hint 'about owning something', matching arimasu-have.
verdictReason: Ledger teaches ありませんでした only as 'there was no / wasn't' (きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありませんでした, かぎはひきだしのなかにありませんでした); the card has no hint and wants 'Did not have'.

claim: The note says again what the front's hint already says.
evidence: Hint on both fronts: 'used to confirm an offer that seems too generous or unexpected'. Note: 'Said when someone makes an unexpected offer, to check they really mean it.'
fix: Drop the note, or use it for something new, such as a typical reply or what the ん in いいんですか is doing.
verdictReason: Hint 'used to confirm an offer that seems too generous or unexpected' and note 'Said when someone makes an unexpected offer, to check they really mean it' say the same thing; the rules say a note must never restate the card.

claim: The note sends the learner to 'GRAMMAR 1–2', a section of a book the learner does not have in Anki.
evidence: Note: 'Marks the giver with もらいます (moraimasu, 'receive from'); with あげます (agemasu) the same に (ni) marks the receiver instead — see GRAMMAR 1–2.'
fix: Remove the 'see GRAMMAR 1–2' pointer; the note already says what it needs to.
verdictReason: The note ends 'see GRAMMAR 1–2', a book section the learner cannot open from Anki, and the note already states the rule. Note for the synthesizer: 27 notes across the collection reference GRAMMAR sections this way, so this is a deck-wide pattern, not a one-card slip.

claim: The note says 'Compare with the previous card', but in a shuffled deck there is no previous card.
evidence: Note: 'Compare with the previous card: あげました (agemashita) and もらいました (moraimashita) describe the same event from the giver's and receiver's side'.
fix: Name the card it means, e.g. 'Compare スミスさんはなかむらさんにはなをあげました'.
verdictReason: The card it means is ks1-ageru-hana (スミスさんはなかむらさんにはなをあげました), which sits one card earlier in cards.json but nowhere in particular in a shuffled deck. One other note in the collection (chapter-9) uses the same 'previous card' phrasing.

claim: 'A friend gave me a scarf.' accepts マフラー as well as スカーフ, because マフラー is glossed 'Muffler, scarf'.
evidence: Production front: 'A friend gave me a scarf.' (answer ともだちがわたしにスカーフをくれました). mafuraa: 'Muffler, scarf', note 'both mean the same thing'.
fix: Fixed by narrowing the マフラー gloss (see the scarf finding); no change to this card needed beyond that.
verdictReason: Production front is 'A friend gave me a scarf.' with no hint, and the mafuraa card glosses マフラー as 'Muffler, scarf' with a note saying both words mean the same thing. Resolved by the merged mafuraa finding (hint on each word card, note rewritten); this card itself needs no edit.

claim: The note only glosses the two parts of the phrase, both of which the learner already has on earlier cards.
evidence: Note: 'おみやげ (omiyage) means souvenir/gift; きょうと (Kyouto) is the city Kyoto.' Ledger: おみやげ 'Souvenir' (Lesson 11), きょうと 'Kyoto' (Lesson 6).
fix: Drop the note.
verdictReason: Ledger has きょうと 'Kyoto' (Lesson 6) and おみやげ 'Souvenir' (Lesson 11); the note only re-glosses the two parts of 'Kyoto souvenir'. Dropping it also clears preflight's romaji finding on this note ('Kyouto' against the deck's 'kyōto').

claim: The romaji writes the long vowel as 'mafuraa', while the word's own card writes 'mafurā'.
evidence: Back: 'Says: Suteki na mafuraa desu ne'. Card mafuraa: 'Says: mafurā'.
fix: Write 'mafurā' here so the romaji matches the vocabulary card.
verdictReason: cards.json pronunciation is 'Suteki na mafuraa desu ne'; the deck's romaji style says long vowels take a macron, never a doubled vowel, and only proper nouns are capitalised, so both 'mafuraa' and the capital S are off style. Preflight's lint did not flag it (it caught only 'ou' doublings in two other fib cards), so this is not already reported.

claim: The note says only four colour words are い-adjectives, but the learner has two more on earlier cards, ちゃいろい and きいろい.
evidence: Note: 'くろい (kuroi) is a true い-adjective, so の never appears here. Same for あかい (akai), あおい (aoi) and しろい (shiroi) — those four and no others.' Ledger, Lesson 5 extras: ちゃいろい 'Brown', きいろい 'Yellow', これはきいろいかさです 'This is a yellow umbrella.'; Lesson 12 extras: これはちゃいろいつくえです 'This is a brown desk.'
fix: Drop 'those four and no others', or say that ちゃいろい and きいろい work the same way while みどり, ピンク and the others take の.
verdictReason: Ledger has きいろい (Lesson 5 extras: 'Yellow is one of only TWO colours with both forms') and ちゃいろい (Lesson 5 extras, Lesson 12 extras) as い-adjectives, so 'those four and no others' contradicts two earlier cards and is false in Japanese. Both roles found it; the Learner's blocker stands because the note teaches something false.

claim: With no owner named and no scene, a learner reads スカーフがありますよ as 'there's a scarf' (Lesson 12), not 'I have a scarf'.
evidence: Recognition front: 'あ、スカーフがありますよ' with no hint; back 'Oh, I have a scarf.' Every other 'have' card names the owner with は (わたしはくるまがあります, わたしはおかねがありません). The note also says 'The chapter's first use of あります as "have"', which means nothing in a shuffle.
fix: Add a scene such as 'offering a scarf to someone who says it is cold', and drop 'the chapter's first use' from the note.
verdictReason: Target lifted verbatim from the dialogue, English is the book's, but cards.json has no scene and without the dialogue スカーフがあります reads as 'there is a scarf' (the Lesson 12 sense). Every other 'have' card in the chapter names the owner. The note's 'The chapter's first use' is meaningless in a shuffle.

claim: 'It's a lovely bag' fits かばん (taught since Lesson 2) as well as バッグ, and the hint does not choose.
evidence: Production front: 'It's a lovely bag, isn't it? Where did you buy it? / complimenting something a friend is carrying' (answer すてきなバッグですね…). Ledger: かばん 'Bag'. Card baggu tells them apart only with its own hint 'a fashion bag like a purse or tote (loanword)'.
fix: Add 'handbag' or 'purse' to the English, or a hint like 'the loanword for a fashion bag'.
verdictReason: Ledger has かばん 'Bag' since Lesson 2; the baggu card separates the two only through its own hint, and this sentence card carries no such cue, so すてきなかばんですね answers the Production front equally well. The book's picture ⑥ is a handbag, so 'handbag' in the English is faithful.

claim: The English says 'evening', which the learner has as ばん, but the answer uses よる, which this chapter glosses 'Night'.
evidence: Production front: 'Do you have time tomorrow evening?' (answer あしたのよるじかんがありますか). Ledger: ばん 'Evening' (Lesson 3), まいばん 'Every evening'. Card yoru: 'Night'. fib-kinyoubi-isogashii-q renders きんようびのよる as 'Friday night'.
fix: Change the English to 'Do you have time tomorrow night?'.
verdictReason: Ledger glosses ばん as 'Evening' (Lesson 3) and まいばん 'Every evening'; よる is first carded in this lesson as 'Night', and fib-kinyoubi-isogashii-q glosses きんようびのよる as 'Friday night'. The sentence is authored for the deck (the book only prints the English instruction), so 'tomorrow night' keeps the deck's own glosses consistent.

claim: The note rules out だれから, which looks like it should work given から 'From', and nothing taught says it is wrong.
evidence: Note: 'だれに, not だれから — with もらいます the giver is marked by に.' Ledger: から 'From (particle)' (Lesson 3).
fix: Say that に is the form this lesson uses for the giver, without calling から wrong (or, if から is accepted, say both work).
verdictReason: Book GRAMMAR 2 teaches に for the giver and says nothing against から; no card in the collection teaches だれから (grep of every cards.json), and ledger has から 'From (particle)' from Lesson 3. The note's 'not だれから' is a prohibition the book does not make and, in general Japanese, もらう does accept から for the giver, so it also risks teaching a false rule.

claim: A learner who has just read that a gift to 'my colleague' takes くれます cannot tell why どうりょう here takes あげます.
evidence: Front: 'どうりょうにあげます / answering who Emma-san will give the ring to'; back '(She) will give it to a colleague.' x14b-tsuma-iyaringu-kuremashita note: 'A gift to my wife, my family or my colleague still counts as coming towards me, so it is くれました and not あげました.' Ledger: どうりょう 'Colleague, coworker'.
fix: Make the English 'to her colleague' so the in-group rule visibly does not apply, or add that line to the note.
verdictReason: The scene names Emma-san as the giver, so あげます is determined (くれます needs the speaker's side as receiver), and the card is correct. The confusion the Learner describes comes from the x14b-tsuma-iyaringu-kuremashita note's 'my colleague' example rather than from this card. Whether '(She) will give it to her colleague' is worth the edit is the owner's call; it is harmless and would settle it.

claim: The question card asks, in the first person, when the asker's own father gives the asker money, while its answer card's scene says it answers about Smith-san's father, so the pair does not fit together.
evidence: fib-chichi-itsu-okane-kuremasu-q: front 'ちちはいつわたしにおかねをくれますか', back 'When does (my) father give me money?'. fib-tanjoubi-ni-kuremasu: scene 'answering when Smith-san's father gives him money', English '(He) gives it to me for my birthday.' Ledger: ちち '(My) father', おとうさん '(Another person's) father'. Both cards are authored for the deck, so the book does not fix the wording.
fix: Rewrite the question so someone asks Smith-san about his father (おとうさんはいつおかねをくれますか, 'When does your father give you money?') and make the answer's scene 'Smith-san answering when his father gives him money'.
verdictReason: Checked both cards: the question is first-person about ちち and わたし, the answer's scene is about Smith-san's father. The answer card itself is sound if Smith is the speaker (くれます with the speaker as receiver), so the edit lands mainly on the question and the scene wording.

claim: 'It's a lovely scarf, isn't it?' can be answered with マフラー, because the deck glosses マフラー 'Muffler, scarf' and its twin card says the same sentence with マフラー.
evidence: Production front: 'It's a lovely scarf, isn't it?' (answer すてきなスカーフですね). Base fib-suteki-mafuraa: 'It's a lovely muffler, isn't it?' → すてきなマフラーですね. mafuraa: 'Muffler, scarf'.
fix: Fixed by narrowing the マフラー gloss (see chapter-14 scarf finding).
verdictReason: fib-suteki-mafuraa (base) is the same sentence with マフラー, and the mafuraa card says the two words mean the same thing. Resolved by the merged mafuraa finding; no separate edit on this card.

claim: The chapter writes the same past negative two ways in romaji, as one word in the base unit and split in the extras.
evidence: Extras: 'kashimasen deshita', 'karimasen deshita', 'agemasen deshita', 'arimasen deshita', 'dōmo sumimasen deshita'. Base: 'kashimasendeshita', 'karimasendeshita', 'agemasendeshita', 'arimasendeshita', 'sumimasendeshita'.
fix: Pick one spacing for -masen deshita and use it across both units.
verdictReason: Counted in the rendered faces: the base unit writes -masendeshita fused in all 22 occurrences and never split; the extras split it in 10 (kashimasen deshita, karimasen deshita, agemasen deshita, dōmo sumimasen deshita, yotei ga arimasen deshita) and fuse it in 8 (e.g. sengetsu yakusoku ga arimasendeshita), so the extras are inconsistent with themselves as well. The style rule lists deshita as a word of its own, which favours the split form. Preflight's lint does not cover this spacing.

claim: The mafuraa note says マフラー and スカーフ mean the same thing, but the book draws and glosses them as two different items; as a result the Production front 'Scarf' (and every sentence card glossed with 'scarf') fits both words and nothing on the front picks one.
evidence: Book, WORD POWER Gifts picture (Page_133_Image_0003): ④ スカーフ is a patterned neck scarf on the woman, ⑨ マフラー a knitted winter scarf on the man; VOCABULARY: 'スカーフ scarf', 'マフラー muffler, scarf'. Card mafuraa: gloss 'Muffler, scarf', note 'A second word for scarf, alongside スカーフ (sukaafu) — both mean the same thing.' Card scarf: Production front 'Clothing / Scarf' with no hint. Sentence cards wanting スカーフ with 'scarf' in the English: kuremasu-example, x14-nakamura-emma-sukaafu-kashimashita, x14-sukaafu-ga-arimasu-yo, x14-suteki-na-sukaafu-desune; fib-suteki-mafuraa wants マフラー for 'muffler'.
fix: Keep the book's gloss 'Muffler, scarf' on mafuraa but rewrite its note: マフラー is the thick knitted winter scarf, スカーフ the light decorative one. Give both word cards a hint (スカーフ 'a light fashion scarf'; マフラー 'a warm knitted winter scarf') so 'scarf' on a Production front resolves to one word; the sentence cards then need no change.
verdictReason: Checked the book picture and glosses: the two items are drawn and glossed differently, so the note's 'both mean the same thing' is not the book's position, and the scarf Production front has no cue. The gloss 'Muffler, scarf' itself is the book's and stays; the fix is the note and a hint on each word card.

claim: The note calls から a suffix, while the book (and the card's own English) call it a particle.
evidence: Book, VOCABULARY: "から because (particle; see NOTES 2)"; NOTES 2: "から is added after an explanatory phrase, signaling a reason for something." Card English: "Because (particle)"; note: "Suffix — attaches after an explanatory clause to give a reason (clause + から (kara))."
fix: Replace "Suffix" with "Particle".
verdictReason: Book VOCABULARY: 'から because (particle; see NOTES 2)'; the card's own English says '(particle)' and the note opens 'Suffix —'. The 'Suffix —' opener is boilerplate in 19 notes across the collection (さん, です), so only the word needs replacing here.

claim: The scene cue says よく is "about how skillfully", but the book teaches it only as the "well" of よく にあいますね (it suits you well), which the card's own note also says.
evidence: Book, EXERCISES VIII VOCABULARY: 'よく にあいますね。 It suits you well.' / 'よく well'. Card hint on both fronts: 'about how skillfully'; card note: 'here it's the manner adverb "well," as in よく にあいますね'. Ledger: よく 'Often' (Lesson 9), the only other よく, so the hint's job is to pick 'well' over 'often'.
fix: Change the hint to something like 'how well something suits or is done (not "often")'.
verdictReason: The book's only use is 'suits you well'; 'skillfully' describes neither that nor anything else this deck teaches for よく, and 'Well' is the only such gloss in the collection, so the hint only needs to separate this よく from Lesson 9's 'often'.
